guest.bio_context: Ryan Sterling is the CEO of NerdWallet Wealth Partners and co-host of Your Next Dollar. He has been in the financial advisory business for two decades and holds all relevant credentials. He works with high-earning clients on wealth management, employee equity, and financial planning, meeting with them on a quarterly basis to provide guidance on their financial decisions.

pending_qa.q: How should spending decisions be framed when considering experiences and relationships?
pending_qa.r: Use the 'last week on earth' test: would you spend the extra money if this were your final opportunity to see someone or have an experience? The host paid $80 instead of $15 for a rental car to see friends on time, a $500 difference that he never regretted because the time with loved ones was irreplaceable. This reframes spending from pure cost-benefit to values-based decision making.

pending_qa.q: What are the mental and professional benefits of international travel for high earners?
pending_qa.r: International travel provides rest, relaxation, and mental clarity that help you return refreshed and ready to execute. Breaking away from routine unlocks ideas and perspectives that daily routines can obscure. The host did not travel internationally until his honeymoon, but over the last decade has made it a priority. Travel also enables quarterly self-evaluation—treating yourself like a public company that reviews earnings and performance each quarter.

pending_qa.q: Why should high earners invest in hiring a financial advisor and CPA?
pending_qa.r: A CPA can identify tax strategies that save thousands annually—the host's CPA found $5,000 in savings in the first year, with that number increasing year over year through quarterly meetings and ongoing strategy discussions. A financial advisor acts as an emotional check, preventing costly mistakes driven by bias and keeping you grounded. Ryan Sterling, despite two decades in finance, uses an advisor because emotions are the number one eroder of wealth, and advisors provide guardrails and clarity.
